text:
mira: quick heads-up — ran a kv-cache fragmentation sweep across us/eu/apac on h100+a100. seeing p99 spikes in eu for mixed-slen workloads, looks region-specific. attaching quick notes below

raj: can you paste the eviction config and the seqlen distribution you used?

mira: sure — eviction=per-gpu-lru-granularity=256, slot_size=32KB, seqlen buckets = [16,64,128,256,512], trace from prod-sample-2026. spikes show up mostly in 128 and 256 buckets.

sasha: suspect fragmentation: when requests with 16/512 mix, we end up with many small holes that prevent 128-sized entries from coalescing. did you enable slot compaction?

mira: not on that run. was trying baseline to compare.

kim: plotted hit-rate vs p99 for eu/h100: p50 stable ~12ms, p95 ~28ms, p99 jumps 85ms for 128/256 mix. us/h100 p99 ~48ms for same mix. a100s show higher avg but lower p99 variance. link: https://redwood-internal/charts/kv-frag/eu-h100 (private)

jordan: number summary i pulled locally:
- us/h100: p50=10ms p95=26ms p99=48ms hitrate=0.82
- eu/h100: p50=12ms p95=30ms p99=85ms hitrate=0.78
- apac/h100: p50=14ms p95=33ms p99=67ms hitrate=0.79
- us/a100: p50=18ms p95=40ms p99=72ms hitrate=0.80

raj: interesting that a100 has higher mean but lower region variance. could be kernel scheduling differences or fragmentation patterns from different placement. do we have kernel/version parity across regions?

mira: eu was on runtime 1.14.2 w/ kernel build rev b3, us/apac had 1.14.5 rev b5. i can rerun eu with b5 to isolate.

ops-bot: experiment run queued: bench/2148765432-evict-compaction-rerun (args: --seq-mix=16,128,512 --compaction=on --gpu=h100 --region=eu)

sasha: aside from compaction, another quick knob is slot_size -> try 64KB so fewer tiny holes for 128 entries. also consider eviction policy: prefer youngest-heavy vs pure-lru for mixed short/long sequences.

kim: ran a microtest with compaction + granularity=128 on eu/h100 — p99 cut from 85ms -> 42ms, hitrate up 3pt. small sample but promising.

jordan: can we add a synthetic trace that amplifies 16/128/512 churn and run across all regions with same runtime? we need to rule out infra differences.

mira: agreed. plan: 1) rerun eu with runtime b5 (raj) 2) run compaction+slot=64k across regions (kim) 3) synthetic churn trace full sweep (jordan) 4) collect kernel traces + evict logs (sasha). targeting results by EOD tomorrow.

raj: i'll start the runtime parity run now, ping if you need creds for eu cluster.

ops-bot: experiment started: bench/2148765432-runtime-parity-eu (eta ~2h)

mira: thanks team — will post consolidated table + small asciichart in this thread when runs finish. if anyone wants to join pairing on analysis, thumbs up here :thumbsup:

kim: :thumbsup: will also export token-dist histograms so we can correlate hole sizes.

jordan: adding a test to flip eviction to size-aware-first (evict smallest hotset) to see impact on p99.

sasha: note for postmortem: also check replica placement — eu has slightly denser allocation pattern which may amplify compaction pauses.

mira: noted. saving logs under s3://redwood-results/kv-frag/2148765432/ — will share links.

raj: great. if compaction proves stable, we should schedule a canary with limited osp traffic then roll to regional pools.

mira: will draft rollout plan after we confirm. thanks everyone.
